headline: De novo sequencing errors trace to limited fragment coverage in MS/MS
label: De Novo Peptide Sequencing Benchmarks
summary: Recent benchmarks and tools expose fragment-evidence limits in de novo sequencing while search and localization methods narrow ambiguity.
synthesis: The common thread is that peptide identification from MS/MS is bounded by fragment-ion evidence. A benchmark of eight deep learning de novo sequencing models on three proteomics datasets reports shared errors arising from limited fragment coverage, indicating that model architecture alone does not resolve sequence ambiguity. Adjacent items address related bottlenecks by constraining the search and localization space: Carafe uses deep learning fragment-ion intensity prediction to prune the Comet fragment ion index, reducing index memory and speeding tandem MS database searches; MS Andrea scores PTM combinations per PSM in open searches using sequence tags; onsite provides alanine-decoy FLR estimation for phosphosite localization; and CasanovoGUI offers a cross-platform desktop interface to Casanovo. What is new is the shift toward narrowing the search space rather than improving sequencing alone, though none of these items explicitly validates fragment-ion evidence as a measured quantity.
